Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
My first Weber grill (Spirit E-310) was purchased in June, 2016.  It was well used approximately 3 times a week for the past 8 years.  I had to replace the flavor bars a couple of times and finally bought stainless steel cooking grates. The grill was easy to clean with a slide-out bottom tray. I would have kept the grill but the burners started to fail.

I bought a new grill (Spirit II E-310) in September, 2024.  Unfortunately, it's a poor replacement.
Cleaning is a real chore with having to remove the cooking grates and flavor bars exposing the delicate burners to potential damage.  Too bad the sides and doors were removed on the current model since it allows easy access to the catch pan for squirrels and other small creatures.
I've used it about 8 times and cleaned it at least 3 times. Yes, I have a cover, also poorly seamed together.

Too bad for us that I didn't want to spend double the price for the better looking, more quality built model.  I'm surprised Webster has its name on such a low-end product.

Let me know if you can make me feel better about this purchase which is registered, yay.
Results.Title: TOO BAD FOR US

Results.ReviewText: My old Weber was approximately 20 years old, had a sturdy frame with square stock and had a removable bottom fire box/pan, never rusted, minimal flare ups, bulky tires, basically heavy duty everything. I didn’t realize until I received my grill that the quality has gone down over the years dramatically. Spending over $500, I expected a lot better. I noticed right away the frame was built cheaper, tires very narrow, could not remove bottom box/pan to clean easily, already have some rust spots after a few weeks with a Weber grill cover, already starting to flare up some. The good news is it does still cook very well. I’m mostly concerned about the longevity of the grill, we cook on it much more than most people and it gets moved a lot as well.
Results.Title: I’m not mad, just disappointed

Results.ReviewText: It’s ok.  Would prefer the left table have the option to be fixed permanent in the up position instead of just swing down.  Don’t like the way you have to manually light the grill.  Would prefer a hole by the far left burner tube so it can be lighted with a lighter that has a 6 inch extension.  When reaching for items on the back of the grill, you have to use gloves or you burn your skin.  Would prefer the bun warmer swing up when the grill is opened so it’s easier to access the items in the back part of the grill.  Electric start is fine, but would prefer the option to install one of those ignition spark makes (when you push down on the button and it creates a spark).  To obtain a temp around 300 - 500˚ F I use only the outside burners (or any two burners), the center burner is turned off.  My son who is not mechanically inclined was able to assemble the grill by reading the instruction.  There were a few steps that seemed out of place around the wiring section, but he managed to assemble the grill.  Recommend removing the battery in the electric starter after use to prevent battery corrosion.  Other than what I mentioned, it’s ok.
Results.Title: What I wish they would change.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: Weber makes an excellent gas grill. I replaced my 16 year old Weber Genesis with this new Spirit II E-310 Weber grill and it's great. However, I have two suggestions for the Weber design team regarding the E-310: The drip pan is too small and awkward to empty without spillage. Needs improvement. After only two weeks of usage, I had a squirrel gnaw through the gas hose in multiple spots resulting in a LP leak during use! I did not notice damage until it was apparent the burners were not getting as hot as usual. Could have been a problem but shut down safely and replaced with Weber part. Also purchased a cover to help deter the pests. I'd like to see a braided hose for durability. Low cost for added safety.
Results.Title: Nice Grill - See Suggestions...

Results.ReviewText:
Pros: My new grill proved very easy to assemble, I like the electric ignition feature. The grill lights quickly and easily. The control valves work smoothly and it is easy to regulate the temperature after a little experience with the grill. I like the thermostat feature in the cover. Cooking on the grill has been a pleasure.
Cons: The scale for the propane bottle is difficult to read.
The propane tank hanger is a bit clumsy to use and the connecting hose does not always line up well to make the gas connection.
In order to move the grill around it is necessary to use the left side table as a handle, I would like to see a more sturdy arrangement to do this.
This grill replaced a 23 year old Weber, I hope it holds up as well as the old one did.
Results.Title: New Grill, Old Cook
